heroHeadline: Russia Kills 8 on Ukraine's Independence Day as Zelensky Vows Ukraine 'Already Defeating Russia'; Kyiv Hits 66 Targets Including Rostov Rocket-Fuel Plant
heroSubtitle: On Ukraine's 35th Independence Day (August 24, 2026), Russia launched a nationwide barrage — 2 Oniks missiles, 6 Kh-31P/Kh-59 guided missiles, and 143 drones — that killed at least 8 and injured 43, with Kharkiv Oblast hit hardest (5 killed, 17 injured); a Russian Geran-5 drone separately struck a residential building in central Chernihiv at midday, injuring 20 including 3 children. President Zelensky used his Independence Day address to declare Ukraine is 'already defeating Russia' and vowed not to cede Donbas to 'save the Kremlin half a million soldiers.' Overnight, Ukrainian drones struck 66 Russian targets, including the Kombinat Kamenskiy rocket-fuel plant in Rostov Oblast, a MiG-29 fighter jet, and three Ozon warehouses; debris from an intercepted drone reportedly killed 2 children at a Krasnodar childcare center. The barrage followed an August 23 day of strikes on Izium and Kharkiv's Osnovianskyi district and a reported Ukrainian strike on an Ozon warehouse in Orenburg, ~1,000km from the border. Russian cumulative personnel losses reached approximately 1,476,580 by August 23, per the Ukrainian General Staff.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Post, Euronews, PBS NewsHour, GlobalSecurity.org, United24 Media, Wikipedia War Timeline, and the Ukrainian General Staff. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
